Region: Steppe north of the Black Sea
History: Scythians were the nomadic steppe peoples north of the Black Sea, proverbial outsiders in the Greek world. Paul names them once, as the far edge of the distinctions abolished in Christ.
Culture: Nomadic horsemen and famed archers, outside the Greek and Jewish worlds alike.
Religion: Steppe gods and customs, far from temple or synagogue.
BibleConnection: Named once, in Paul's list of distinctions — Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, Barbarian, Scythian — that do not divide those renewed in Christ.
